response.sql: SELECT t.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandwidth_usage_pct, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.observstation IN (SELECT t2.observstation FROM telescopes t2 WHERE t2.equipstatus IS NOT NULL AND t2.equipstatus <> 'Maintenance') GROUP BY t.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC, station, moon_phase LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The equipment-status filter works at station level: a station qualifies if it has at least one telescope with a non-NULL equipstatus other than 'Maintenance', and then all of that station's matched telescopes are counted, including any in Maintenance.
Telescopes with no matching observatory are dropped by the inner join on observstation.
Telescopes whose observatory has a NULL lunarstage are kept as their own 'moon phase' group rather than dropped, since the request does not exclude them.
AVG() skips NULL bandusagepct values, which satisfies 'ignoring missing values'. COUNT(*) counts every telescope in the group, including those with a NULL bandusagepct.
Ties in telescope_count are broken by station and then moon phase so the top 10 is deterministic. The request does not specify a tie-break.

alternatives.interpretation: The equipment-status filter applies to individual telescopes rather than stations: only telescopes whose equipstatus is recorded and not 'Maintenance' are counted, so Maintenance telescopes are excluded from the averages and counts.
alternatives.sql: SELECT t.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandwidth_usage_pct, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.equipstatus IS NOT NULL AND t.equipstatus <> 'Maintenance' GROUP BY t.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC, station, moon_phase LIMIT 10;
